inputs.text: The real issue is who gets protected when energy prices spike. Workers and low-income households shouldn’t be left carrying the costs of a crisis they didn’t create, while the wealthy are better positioned to absorb the shock. Cutting fuel duties may help briefly, but it isn’t justice if the bill later comes through weaker public services or other burdens on ordinary people. India’s dependence on imported crude makes the need for a fair, resilient energy transition even more urgent—one that protects livelihoods and makes those with the greatest resources contribute fairly.

output.main_topic: Fairness and protection in responding to energy price spikes
subtopics: Fuel duty cuts and public service costs
